summary: Phase 1 of the myidsan productization plan: passphrase-encrypted backup and restore for the whole identity store, closing the gap where the only documented disaster-recovery procedure was "copy the database and secret/atrest.key yourself, as a pair." A new superadmin-only surface (GET /api/backup/sections, POST /api/backup/{export,preview,restore}, not delegatable through the RBAC permission matrix even by grant) produces or consumes a single `.idbackup` file covering six ordered, selectable sections: access (roles/permissions), identity (users/groups/avatars), MFA (TOTP factors/recovery codes), apps (registry/auth config/redirect URIs), federation (directory config/group mappings), and the SSO CA. The design point that makes a restore usable on a different machine: the two at-rest-sealed values (TOTP secrets, the LDAP bind password) are unsealed on export and re-sealed with the destination host's own at-rest key on restore, so the archive is never a dead end (a naive sealed-bytes copy would restore cleanly and then fail every second-factor check) -- the at-rest key itself never travels. Restore remaps every foreign key onto freshly-created destination ids and skips any row whose parent wasn't restored rather than leaving a dangling or reinterpreted grant, drops every live session afterward (a pre-restore session would still carry pre-restore authority), and marks first-run setup complete. Reachable from a new Backup & restore page in the nav and from a new "restore from a backup instead" path on the first-run wizard's welcome step. Verified end-to-end against a live instance: enrol MFA, export, destroy the database and the at-rest key, fresh-install, restore, sign in with the pre-disaster password, redeem a TOTP code generated from the pre-disaster secret.
compatibility: New tables/entities are additive; nothing is removed or restructured. The feature is opt-in and has no effect on an install that never uses it -- no scheduled/automatic backup runs on its own. The passphrase is the only thing protecting the exported file (it carries password hashes, TOTP secrets, and a CA private key); a minimum of 12 characters is enforced on export. Restore is inherently destructive by design in its default 'replace' mode (it wipes each selected section's own tables before inserting) and always invalidates every live session including the operator's own, by design -- this is documented as expected in deploy/README-myidsan.md's new DR runbook rather than a bug.
